text:
The minimum energy that must be possessed by photons in order to produce the photoelectric effect with platinum metal is :

[Given : The threshold frequency of platinum is 1.3 $\times$ $10^{15} s^{-1}$ and h = 6.6 $\times$ $10^{-34} J s$.]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The minimum energy possessed by photons will be
equal to the work function of the metal.

$\therefore$ $E_{\min } = hν_{0}$ J

= 6.6 $\times$ $10^{-34}$ $\times$ 1.3 $\times$ $10^{15}$

= 8.58 $\times$ $10^{-19} J$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: At 25${}^{\circ }$C and 1 atm pressure, the enthalpy of combustion of benzene (l) and acetylene (g) are $-$ 3268 kJ mol$^{-1}$ and $-$1300 kJ mol$^{-1}$, respectively. The change in enthalpy for the reaction $3 C_{2}H_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $C_{6}H_{6} (l)$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given: $\Delta _{c}H^{\circ }(\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{6},l)=-3268\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta _{c}H^{\circ }(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{2},g)=-1300\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

$\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{5}{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\Delta H_{1}=-1300\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}(\mathrm{l})+\frac{15}{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow 6\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+3\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})\Delta H_{2}=-3268\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Three times the first equation minus the second cancels $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$, $\mathrm{CO}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ and leaves $3~\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow \mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}(\mathrm{l})$. So, with combustion enthalpies, $\Delta _{r}H=\sum \Delta _{c}H(\text{reactants})-\sum \Delta _{c}H(\text{products})$:

$\Delta _{r}H=3\Delta H_{1}-\Delta H_{2}=3(-1300)-(-3268)=-3900+3268=-632\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text:
Solute A associates in water. When 0.7 g of solute A is dissolved in 42.0 g of water, it depresses the freezing point by 0.2${}^{\circ }$C. The percentage association of solute A in water, is :

[Given : Molar mass of A = 93 g mol$^{-1}$. Molal depression constant of water is 1.86 K kg mol$^{-1}$.]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since, $\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{f}}=\mathrm{ik}_{\mathrm{f}}m$

$\begin{array}{l} m=\dfrac{0.7}{93}\times \dfrac{1000}{42} \\  \\ 0.2=i\times 1.86\times \dfrac{0.7\times 1000}{93\times 42} \\  \\ i=0.6 \\  \\ α=\dfrac{i-1}{\frac{1}{n}-1}=\dfrac{0.6-1}{\frac{1}{2}-1}=0.8 \end{array}$

Hence, the percentage association of solute $A$ is $80%$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: The correct order of electron gain enthalpies of Cl, F, Te and Po is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electron gain enthalpies (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$): Cl $-349$, F $-328$, Te $-190$, Po $-174$.

F releases less energy than Cl because its small, compact 2p shell repels the incoming electron strongly, and Te and Po release much less because of their larger size and lower effective attraction for the added electron.

Ordered by the magnitude of energy released on gaining an electron: Po < Te < F < Cl.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R :

Assertion A : The amphoteric nature of water is explained by using Lewis acid/base concept.

Reason R : Water acts as an acid with $NH_{3}$ and as a base with $H_{2}S$.

In the light of the above statements choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The amphoteric nature of water is explained by
using Bronsted-Lowry acid base concept

$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{\text{(acid)}}+\mathrm{NH}_{3}⇌\mathrm{OH}^{-}+\mathrm{NH}_{4}^{+}$

$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{\text{(base)}}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{S}⇌\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}+\mathrm{HS}^{-}$

Hence, A is false but R is true
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text:
The correct order of reduction potentials of the following pairs is

$A. Cl_{2}/Cl^{-}$

$B. I_{2}/I^{-}$

$C. Ag^{+}/Ag$

$D. Na^{+}/Na$

$E. Li^{+}/Li$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Standard reduction potentials of the couples:

$E_{\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}/\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}}^{\circ }=+1.36\text{V},E_{\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag}}^{\circ }=+0.80\text{V},E_{\mathrm{I}{}_{2}/\mathrm{I}{}^{-}}^{\circ }=+0.54\text{V}$

$E_{\mathrm{Na}{}^{+}/\mathrm{Na}}^{\circ }=-2.71\text{V},E_{\mathrm{Li}{}^{+}/\mathrm{Li}}^{\circ }=-3.05\text{V}$

In decreasing order, $+1.36>+0.80>+0.54>-2.71>-3.05$, i.e. A > C > B > D > E. $\mathrm{Ag}{}^{+}/\mathrm{Ag}$ lies above $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}/\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$, and Li lies below Na because of the very large hydration enthalpy of the small $\mathrm{Li}{}^{+}$ ion.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text:
Amongst the following, the major product of the given chemical reaction is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Bromine adds to the C=C of 3,4-dihydro-2H-pyran to form a cyclic bromonium ion across C-2 and C-3, where C-2 is the carbon bonded to the ring oxygen.

The lone pair of the ring oxygen stabilises positive charge on C-2 (oxocarbenium character), so C-2 is the carbon attacked by the nucleophile.

Methanol is the solvent and is present in large excess, so it opens the bromonium ion at C-2; loss of $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ leaves an $\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ group on C-2 and Br on C-3.

The attack occurs from the face opposite the bromonium bridge (anti addition), so $\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ on C-2 and Br on C-3 are trans to each other.


[IMG]

The major product is trans-3-bromo-2-methoxytetrahydropyran, with $\mathrm{OCH}{}_{3}$ (wedge) on the carbon next to O and Br (hashed bond) on the adjacent carbon. Option (B) is the cis isomer, and options (C) and (D) place Br on the carbon next to O.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: Which of the following conditions or reaction sequence will NOT give acetophenone as the major product?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Methylmagnesium bromide adds to benzaldehyde; hydrolysis gives the secondary alcohol 1-phenylethanol, which acidified dichromate oxidises to acetophenone:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CHO}{}_{\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}}^{\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{\mathrm{Na}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cr}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7},\mathrm{H}{}^{+}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$

(B) Phenylmagnesium bromide adds to ethanal to give the same 1-phenylethanol, which PCC in dichloromethane oxidises to acetophenone:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CHO}{}_{\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}}^{\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{MgBr}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}{}^{\mathrm{PCC}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$

(C) An ester consumes two equivalents of Grignard reagent: the first addition expels $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{O}{}^{-}$ and forms acetophenone, but this ketone is more reactive than the ester and adds the second $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ at once, so the product is the tertiary alcohol 2-phenylpropan-2-ol:

$\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COOC}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}{}_{\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}}^{2\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}}\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$

(D) $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ and $\mathrm{CdCl}{}_{2}$ form dimethylcadmium, which converts the acid chloride to the ketone and, being much less reactive than a Grignard reagent, does not attack the ketone:

$2~\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}+\mathrm{CdCl}{}_{2}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cd}+2\mathrm{MgBrCl}$

$2~\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COCl}+(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{Cd}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}+\mathrm{CdCl}{}_{2}$

Only sequence (C) fails to give acetophenone as the major product.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: A protein 'A' contains 0.30% of glycine (molecular weight 75). The minimum molar mass of the protein 'A' is $__________$ $\times$ $10^{3} g$ mol$^{-1}$ [nearest integer]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The molar mass of protein A is least when each molecule contains the smallest possible amount of glycine, that is, exactly one glycine unit (molar mass $75\text{g mol}^{-1}$) per molecule.

Glycine then makes up $0.30%$ of the minimum molar mass $M_{\text{\min }}$:

$\dfrac{0.30}{100}\times M_{\text{\min }}=75$

$M_{\text{\min }}=\dfrac{75\times 100}{0.30}=25000\text{g mol}^{-1}=25\times 10^{3}\text{g mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 25.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: At 345 K, the half life for the decomposition of a sample of a gaseous compound initially at 55.5 kPa was 340 s. When the pressure was 27.8 kPa, the half life was found to be 170 s. The order of the reaction is $____________$. [integer answer]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$t_{1/2}\propto \frac{1}{[P_{0}]^{n-1}}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\left (\mathrm{t}_{1/2}\right )_{1}}{\left (\mathrm{t}_{1/2}\right )_{2}}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{P}_{0}]_{2}^{\mathrm{n}-1}}{[\mathrm{P}_{0}]_{1}^{\mathrm{n}-1}} \\  \\ \dfrac{340}{170}=\left (\dfrac{27.8}{55.5}\right )^{\mathrm{n}-1} \\  \\ 2=\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )^{\mathrm{n}-1} \\  \\ 2=(2)^{1-n} \\  \\ 1-\mathrm{n}=1 \\  \\ \mathrm{n}=0 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text:
A solution of $Fe_{2}(SO_{4})_{3}$ is electrolyzed for 'x' min with a current of 1.5 A to deposit 0.3482 g of Fe. The value of x is $___________$. [nearest integer]

Given : 1 F = 96500 C mol$^{-1}$

Atomic mass of Fe = 56 g mol$^{-1}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+3\mathrm{e}^{-}\to \mathrm{Fe}$

$\text{Moles of Fe deposited}=\frac{0.3482}{56}=6.2\times 10^{-3}$

For 1 mole $\mathrm{Fe}$, charge required is $3\mathrm{F}$

For $6.2\times 10^{-3}$ mole $\mathrm{Fe}$, charge required is $3\times 6.2\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{F}$

Since, charge required $=18.6\times 10^{-3}\times 96500\mathrm{C}$

$=1794.9\mathrm{C}$

And,

$1.5\times \mathrm{t}=1794.9$

$t=\frac{1794.9}{1.5\times 60}\min$

$\mathrm{t}\simeq 20\min$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text: Amongst FeCl$_{3}.3H_{2}O, K_{3}$[$Fe(CN)_{6}$] and [$Co(NH_{3})_{6}$]$Cl_{3}$, the spin-only magnetic moment value of the inner-orbital complex that absorbs light at shortest wavelength is $____________ B.M$. [nearest integer]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{3}\mathrm{Cl}_{3}]\to$ Outer-orbital complex

$\mathrm{K}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]\to \text{Inner-orbital complex}$

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}_{3}\to$ Inner-orbital complex

Since $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ is a stronger field ligand than $\mathrm{NH}_{3}$. Hence $\mathrm{K}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_{6}]$ is the inner-orbital complex that absorbs light at shortest wavelength.

$\mathrm{Fe}(\text{III})\to$ valence shell configuration $3\mathrm{d}^{5}$

Since $\mathrm{CN}^{-}$ will do pairing, so unpaired electron $=1$

$μ=\sqrt{1(1+2)}=\sqrt{3}\mathrm{BM}\simeq 2\mathrm{BM}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift

text:
The neutralization occurs when 10 mL of 0.1M acid 'A' is allowed to react with 30 mL of 0.05 M base $M(OH)_{2}$. The basicity of the acid 'A' is $__________$.

[M is a metal]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Milieq of acid $A=$ Milieq of base $M(OH)_{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} (\mathrm{M}\times \mathrm{V}\times \mathrm{n}-\text{Factor}_{A}=(\mathrm{M}\times \mathrm{V}\times \mathrm{n}-\text{Factor})_{\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}} \\  \\ [\mathrm{n}-\text{Factor of}\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}=2] \\  \\ 0.1\times 10\times \mathrm{n}\text{-Factor}=0.05\times 30\times 2 \\  \\ (\mathrm{n}-\text{Factor})_{\mathrm{A}}=3 \end{array}$

Hence basicity of acid $A$ is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th June Evening Shift
